memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was not willing to let them go. Pharaoh said to Moses, "Get out of my sight! Make sure you do not appear before me again! The day you see my face you will die." "Just as you say," Moses replied. "I will never appear before you again."" - Exodus 10:27-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The negotiations end here. Pharaoh throws Moses out with a threat: the day you see my face you will die.

Moses' reply is calm and final. Just as you say. I will never appear before you again.

There is a solemn finality in this exchange. Pharaoh has slammed the door for the last time, and God will not send another delegation. The next word from heaven will be judgement.

That is sobering. God's patience is enormous — nine plagues, repeated warnings, mercy after every broken promise. But patience is not the same as permanence. There does come a point where a person's final answer is accepted.

We should not read this fearfully but urgently. Scripture says now is the time of God's favour, now is the day of salvation (2 Cor 6:2). The invitation is genuinely open today.

Notice too Moses' composure. No anger, no last plea, no fear of the threat. He had done everything God asked. He could walk away with a clear conscience.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I treating God's patience as though it will last forever?
2. Is there anything God has asked of me that I have left undone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want to presume on Your patience. Whatever You are asking of me, I answer You today. Amen.
